name: US inflation
summary: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October; index data imply about 4.1% annual inflation, inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band
state: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected (CNBC, 10 Nov). FRED index data imply annual CPI inflation of about 4.1% for October, up from 4.0% in September and rising for three months, inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band and below the 4.5% Alert line (FRED). November CPI is due in mid-December.
for_you: Higher inflation erodes the value of wages and savings and tends to keep borrowing costs elevated. Households on fixed incomes and those refinancing debt are most exposed.
rubric_hit: CPI 4.1% y/y within 3.0–4.5% Watch band and rising 3 months; below 4.5% Alert line

sources.title: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL)
Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected, complicating Fed's inflation fight

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
